walkthroughs.body_html: Salmonella is linked to raw eggs and poultry. Campylobacter is the most common cause of UK food poisoning, mostly from undercooked chicken. E. coli O157 can come from undercooked beef or unwashed salad and is potentially serious.

The UK Food Safety Act 1990 makes it a criminal offence to sell unsafe food. The Food Standards Agency (FSA) inspects businesses, gives them a hygiene rating (0-5) and can close premises. Records under HACCP support legal compliance.

UK law requires food businesses to declare 14 named allergens in any food they sell — including nuts, peanuts, eggs, milk, gluten, soya, fish, crustaceans, molluscs, celery, mustard, sesame, sulphites and lupin. Cross-contamination of allergens is a serious safety issue.
